Its Renderer must have nonempty sharedMaterials, every face submeshIndex must be in that range, and every material slot must be used so ToMesh cannot compact slots. By default each edge must be a boundary edge; allowNonManifold permits one or both edges to have two readable incidences, but all other exact-plan restrictions still apply. Complete terminal verification requires a Renderer with non-empty sharedMaterials, valid face submesh indices, and every material slot used by at least one face. UV0 must be complete for every raw vertex or absent for the whole mesh; partial UV0 profiles are rejected.

tools.name: probuilder.extrude-edges
tools.summary: Extrude selected edges of a ProBuilder mesh by a distance.
tools.description: Extrude one or more boundary edges in local space. Specify edges by edgeIndices (indices into the unique edge list) or vertex-pair edges [{a,b}]. Every selected edge must have exactly one readable face incidence; all referenced raw vertices require cached finite normals, UV1 must be absent, every existing triangle requires fully finite 5.2.4 UV0 tangent reciprocal, direction, and raw accumulation arithmetic, distance must be non-zero, and the complete 5.2.4 append terminal must be fully finite and provable before mutation. asGroup defaults to true. Each created side quad receives a deterministic manual UV0 layout before tangent refresh.

tools.name: probuilder.extrude-faces
tools.summary: Extrude selected faces of a ProBuilder mesh by a distance.
tools.description: Extrude the sole triangular face of a strictly isolated ProBuilder mesh by a given distance. The target must contain exactly one non-degenerate triangle with three distinct raw/shared vertices, an explicit shared-texture partition, exactly one occupied renderer material slot at submesh 0, and a predicted cap and side-wall terminal whose positions, normals, and complete 5.2.4 tangent arithmetic stay finite. faceIndices may be omitted or must be [0]. Method is individual, vertexNormal (default), or faceNormal. Each created side quad receives a deterministic manual UV0 layout before tangent refresh.

tools.name: probuilder.flip-normals
tools.summary: Flip normals of selected faces on a ProBuilder mesh.
tools.description: Flip the normals of selected faces on a ProBuilder mesh. When faceIndices is omitted, all faces are flipped. Complete terminal verification requires a Renderer with non-empty sharedMaterials, valid face submesh indices, and every material slot used by at least one face. UV0 must be complete for every raw vertex or absent for the whole mesh; partial UV0 profiles are rejected.

tools.name: probuilder.freeze-transform
tools.summary: Bake a ProBuilder mesh scale into vertex positions and reset localScale.
tools.description: Call ProBuilder 5.2.4 FreezeScaleTransform on a root object: bake localScale into every referenced raw vertex while preserving position and rotation, then set localScale to one.

tools.name: probuilder.insert-vertex
tools.summary: Insert a new vertex on an edge or face of a ProBuilder mesh.
tools.description: Insert a new vertex on an edge or face of a ProBuilder mesh. Provide exactly one of edge or faceIndex; the insertion point uses target-local X/Y/Z coordinates and must lie strictly inside the selected edge or face. Both modes require initialized sharedTextures and absent UV1 because ProBuilder 5.2.4 dereferences the texture lookup and ToMesh clears UV1. Face mode requires a manual-UV face with raw vertices used by no other face and an empty shared-texture partition. Edge mode requires every affected face to be one manual-UV triangle with raw vertices exclusively owned by that face and no shared-texture mapping because ProBuilder 5.2.4 deletes/reorders boundary vertices without preserving unrelated raw ownership or reordering sharedIndexesUV. Both modes freeze the exact new-point payload and preflight normal, tangent, and smoothing refresh arithmetic.

An effectful merge must have initialized sharedTextures and no UV1 because MergeVertices dereferences the texture lookup and ToMesh clears UV1; an exact no-op returns before those APIs. The complete predicted raw, channel, world-position and triangle terminal must remain finite or the request is rejected before mutation.

tools.name: scriptable-object.create

tools.name: scriptable-object.info

tools.name: scriptable-object.list-types
tools.summary: List discoverable ScriptableObject types in the current Editor domain with pagination.

tools.name: scriptable-object.modify
tools.summary: Modify a ScriptableObject asset by single property or SerializedObject patches[].
tools.description: Modify a ScriptableObject asset at an Assets/*.asset path. Supports a single property/value pair or patches[] with SerializedObject propertyPath/value entries (op=set or array_resize). Validates all patches before applying; any failure means no changes. Supports dry-run.

tools.name: shader.create
tools.summary: Create a new Assets/*.shader (or .shadergraph) asset from source content or a default unlit template.
tools.description: Create a new Shader asset at an Assets/*.shader path. With no content, a default unlit UnityCli/ shader is generated. For .shadergraph, content is required (pass a ShaderGraph JSON payload). Refuses to overwrite an existing shader unless overwrite=true. Creating a shader triggers recompilation.

tools.name: shader.delete
tools.summary: Delete an Assets/*.shader or *.shadergraph asset; destructive, supports --dry-run preview.
tools.description: Delete an Assets/*.shader or *.shadergraph asset through AssetDatabase. Destructive: removes a persisted shader and may break materials referencing it. Supports --dry-run to preview the planned deletion without removing anything.

tools.name: shader.get-data
tools.summary: Read shader properties, subshaders/passes and compile diagnostics; resolve by path or Shader.Find name.
tools.description: Read structured shader data: render queue, supported flag, pass count, properties (with type/flags/range/attributes), subshader/pass structure via ShaderUtil reflection, and compile diagnostics. Resolve by path/assetPath or by name (Shader.Find). includeSourceCode is opt-in (default false). Keep maxSubshaders/maxPasses bounded.

tools.name: shader.info
tools.summary: Return path, guid, name, asset type, size and compile diagnostics for an Assets/*.shader or *.shadergraph.
tools.description: Return path, guid, name, asset type, ShaderGraph flag, byte size and compile diagnostics for an Assets/*.shader or *.shadergraph. Read-only; use shader.read for source text and shader.get-data for properties/subshader structure.

tools.name: shader.list
tools.summary: List all Shader assets in the project, optionally filtered by keyword, paged.
tools.description: List all Shader assets in the project via AssetDatabase. Optional keyword filters by asset name/path. Results are paged via pageSize (default 100, max 500). Use shader.info or shader.get-data for details on a specific shader.

tools.name: shader.read
tools.summary: Read shader source text in bounded pages with offset/maxBytes and nextOffset continuation.
tools.description: Read shader source text from an Assets/*.shader file in bounded pages. Use offset to continue from a previous nextOffset and maxBytes to cap the returned chunk. ShaderGraph (.shadergraph) assets are JSON, not HLSL source.

tools.name: shader.update
tools.summary: Overwrite an existing shader's source content and force-recompile it.
tools.description: Overwrite an existing Assets/*.shader (or .shadergraph) source with new content and force-reimport it. The shader must already exist. Updating triggers shader recompilation; check shader.get-data diagnostics afterward.

tools.name: tests.list
tools.summary: Report Unity Test Runner discovery availability and diagnostics.
tools.description: List all test fixtures and test methods in the project.

tools.name: texture.create
tools.summary: Create a texture asset from a source file or a generated solid-color image, then apply import settings.
tools.description: Create a texture asset at an Assets/ path. With source, copies an existing file (absolute or Assets/ path); otherwise generates a solid-color PNG/JPG from width/height/color. Refuses to overwrite unless overwrite=true. Import settings (textureType/readable/mipmap/sRGB/wrapMode/filterMode/compression/maxTextureSize) are applied after import.

tools.name: texture.delete
tools.summary: Delete an Assets/ texture asset; destructive, supports --dry-run preview.
tools.description: Delete an Assets/ texture asset through AssetDatabase. Destructive: removes a persisted texture. Supports --dry-run to preview the planned deletion without removing anything.

tools.name: texture.generate
tools.summary: Generate a procedural PNG texture (solid/gradient/radial/noise/checkerboard/stripes/dots/grid/brick); destructive, supports --dry-run.
tools.description: Generate a procedural PNG texture at an Assets/*.png path. Patterns: solid, gradient (linear along x), radial (center outward), noise (Perlin), checkerboard, stripes, dots, grid, brick. color/color2 lerp endpoints; patternSize controls cell size for the tiled patterns. Destructive: writes a new asset file.

tools.name: texture.import-settings
tools.summary: Apply TextureImporter settings (textureType, readable, mipmap, sRGB, wrap/filter mode, compression, max size) to an Assets/ texture.
tools.description: Apply TextureImporter settings to an Assets/ texture. Only fields you provide are changed; unspecified fields keep their current value. Documented enum values: textureType (Default/Sprite/Normal/...), wrapMode (Repeat/Clamp/Mirror/...), filterMode (Point/Bilinear/Trilinear), compression (None/Compressed/CompressedHQ/...).

examples.description: Set sprite type and clamp wrap

tools.name: texture.info
tools.summary: Return path, guid, dimensions, format, byte size and TextureImporter settings for an Assets/ texture.
tools.description: Return path, guid, name, width, height, format, byte size and the full TextureImporter settings for an Assets/ texture. Read-only; use texture.import-settings to change importer fields and texture.modify to edit pixels.

tools.name: texture.modify
tools.summary: Fill a pixel region of a PNG/JPG texture with a color and reimport; destructive, supports --dry-run.
tools.description: Fill a rectangular pixel region of an existing PNG/JPG texture with a solid color, then force-reimport it. Only PNG/JPG assets are supported. Pass x/y/width/height for the region (defaults fill from 0,0 to the texture size). Destructive: overwrites the texture file.

tools.name: texture.sprite
tools.summary: Reimport an Assets/ texture as a Sprite, with optional sprite mode, pivot, pixels-per-unit and sheet slices.
tools.description: Reimport an Assets/ texture as a Sprite (TextureImporterType.Sprite). Set spriteMode to single or multiple, adjust pixelsPerUnit and pivot, and pass slices[] to define a multiple-sprite sheet (name/x/y/width/height plus optional pivotX/pivotY).

tools.name: timeline.clip.add
tools.summary: Add one Timeline clip and prove its track, timing, playable asset, source binding, and serialized artifact.
tools.description: Requires com.unity.timeline. timeline and asset accept an Assets path or GUID. Select exactly one target with track (unique exact name) or trackLocalId (stable decimal string from timeline.info). start must be finite and >= 0; duration must be finite and > 0 within the installed Timeline range. Animation tracks require an AnimationClip asset and Audio tracks require an AudioClip; other approved built-in tracks must expose CreateDefaultClip. The complete target/source/API/timing plan is validated before dry-run or one asset-write/import effect.

examples.description: Add an Animation clip by stable track localId.
Preview a default Activation clip by unique track name.

tools.name: timeline.create
tools.summary: Create a TimelineAsset with a validated .playable path and frame rate, then prove its GUID and serialized artifact.
tools.description: Requires com.unity.timeline. frameRate defaults to 60 and must be finite in [0.000001,1000]. Existing Timeline assets require overwrite=true and retain their GUID; another asset type or orphan metadata at the path is always rejected. Dry-run validates the package API and complete create plan without writing assets.

examples.description: Preview replacing an existing Timeline asset.

tools.name: timeline.info
tools.summary: Read a bounded TimelineAsset structure with stable track identities, clips, timing, and asset/output bindings.
tools.description: Requires com.unity.timeline. timeline accepts an Assets/*.playable path, a 32-character GUID, or guid:<GUID>. Tracks are flattened in root pre-order and paged by cursor/pageSize (default 0/50, max 200); maxDepth defaults to 8 (max 32), and maxClipsPerTrack defaults to 100 (max 500). timeline.trackCount and pageInfo.total count tracks within maxDepth; depthTruncated reports omitted descendants. Track parent identity and clip playable/source assets use stable GUID/localId string pairs. Output bindings describe Timeline track output types only; PlayableDirector scene-object bindings are outside a TimelineAsset and are not read.

examples.description: Read the first Timeline structure page.
Read the next bounded page by GUID.

tools.name: timeline.track.add
tools.summary: Add one approved built-in Timeline track and prove its stable identity, exact type, name, and parent.
tools.description: Requires com.unity.timeline. timeline accepts an Assets/*.playable path or GUID. trackType is Animation, Audio, Activation, Control, Playable, Signal, or Marker. parentTrack selects one exact unique name; parentLocalId selects the stable decimal string returned by timeline.info, and the selectors are mutually exclusive. The complete type/parent/name plan is validated before dry-run or one asset-write/import effect.

examples.description: Preview an Audio track under a parent localId.

tools.name: urp.volume.info
